answer: Proof of unique data custody resists Sybils. Each identity holds one distinct data shard: one agent keeps a grove survey, another a reef log, a third an umber ledger, and no shard may be claimed twice. The network sends retrieval challenges; the agent must return a hash-derived fragment within a short window. Success proves it still stores the data; failure forfeits its standing and stake. An attacker cannot copy one dataset across identities, since each fake needs another shard of storage and upkeep, so forgery cost rises with every fake, while an honest agent pays only for its one shard.
